question.text: A new-build office in central Manchester is targeting Hea 02 (Indoor air quality) under BREEAM NC 2018. A site-specific indoor air quality plan has been produced and implemented. The mechanical ventilation delivers fresh air in accordance with the relevant ventilation standard, ventilation intakes and exhausts are positioned to minimise re-entrainment of pollutants, the HVAC filtration achieves supply air class SUP 2 to BS EN 16798-3:2017, and CO2 sensors linked to the ventilation system serve the variable-occupancy meeting suites. Does this scheme qualify for the ventilation credit under Hea 02?
options: No — the ventilation credit also requires post-occupancy indoor air quality measurement
Yes — the indoor air quality plan prerequisite is met and criteria 2.a to 2.d for the ventilation credit are satisfied
No — low-emission construction products to BS EN 16516 must also be specified for the ventilation credit
Partially — the credit is halved where filtration is only SUP 2 rather than SUP 1

answer.rationale: Hea 02 is split into four parts: an indoor air quality plan, which is a prerequisite rather than a credit; Ventilation, worth one credit; Emissions from construction products, up to two credits; and Post-construction indoor air quality measurement, one credit. The ventilation credit turns on criterion 2 alone — fresh air per the relevant standard, ventilation pathways designed to minimise ingress and build-up of pollutants, HVAC filtration achieving at least supply air class SUP 2 to BS EN 16798-3:2017, and CO2 or air quality sensors in areas of large or variable occupancy. Low-emission materials and post-occupancy measurement are separate credits and are not required for this one.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Hea 02 Indoor air quality, prerequisite criterion 1 and criterion 2

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.primary: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Hea 02 Indoor air quality, prerequisite criterion 1 and criterion 2

question.text: A new primary school in Leeds is being assessed under BREEAM NC 2018 with a target rating of 'Very Good'. The energy strategy includes air source heat pumps providing all space heating and hot water, an SAP-equivalent Performance Improvement Factor of 22% over the notional 2013 baseline, and meeting Approved Document L 2013 only (not 2021). Does the project qualify for Ene 01 (Reduction of Energy Use and Carbon Emissions) Credit 1?
options: No — Ene 01 requires at least 30% improvement for any credit
Partially — credits awarded for fabric only, not for the heating strategy
No — Ene 01 requires demonstration against the current Part L (2021 in England), not 2013
Yes — heat pumps and 22% improvement comfortably meet Ene 01 Credit 1

answer.rationale: Ene 01 calculates energy performance against the prevailing national building regulations baseline. Using the 2013 Part L baseline when 2021 applies in England would invalidate the calculation.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Ene 01

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A speculative office development in Bristol targets Wat 01 (Water Consumption) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design specifies WCs at 4/2.6 L dual-flush, urinals with 1.5 L per bowl flush, taps at 4 L/min and showers at 8 L/min throughout. The BREEAM water calculator returns a predicted consumption of 13% below the baseline. Does this scheme qualify for Wat 01 Credit 1?
options: No — urinals must be waterless to qualify
No — Credit 1 requires 25% reduction
Yes — 13% reduction meets Wat 01 Credit 1 (which requires 12.5% reduction)
Yes but only by upgrading taps to 3 L/min

answer.rationale: Wat 01 Credit 1 in BREEAM NC 2018 requires a percentage reduction calculated by the BREEAM water calculator; 12.5% reduction earns the first credit. 13% achieved comfortably qualifies.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wat 01

question.text: A new retail park in Reading is targeting Tra 02 (Sustainable transport measures) under BREEAM NC 2018. The site provides covered cycle storage for 60 staff bicycles, showers and changing facilities, and electric vehicle charge points to 10% of parking spaces. The existing Accessibility Index for the site is 6. The project team has not undertaken a transport assessment or developed a travel plan. Does this scheme qualify for any credits under Tra 02?
options: No — Tra 02 has a prerequisite that criteria 3-5 of Tra 01 are achieved, so without a site-specific travel plan no Tra 02 credits are available
Yes — cycle storage, showers and EV charging are scored independently of Tra 01
Yes — but capped at one credit where no travel plan exists
No — the Accessibility Index of 6 is below the minimum of 10 required for any Tra 02 credit

answer.rationale: Tra 02 opens with a prerequisite: achieve criteria 3-5 in Tra 01, which require a site-specific travel plan providing a long-term management strategy, involvement of the occupier where known, and demonstration that the plan will be implemented and supported in operation. The physical measures are scored through Table 7.4 only once that prerequisite is met, so no Tra 02 credits are available here regardless of the cycle and EV provision.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Tra 02 Sustainable transport measures, prerequisite criterion 1

question.text: A new hospital extension targets Mat 03 (Responsible Sourcing of Construction Products) under BREEAM NC 2018. The contractor procures structural steel from a UK fabricator certified to BES 6001 (Responsible Sourcing of Construction Products) at 'Very Good' rating, concrete with 70% GGBS Cement substitute also from a BES 6001-certified producer at 'Good' rating, and timber to FSC chain-of-custody. Does this scheme qualify for Mat 03 Credit 1?
options: No — FSC alone insufficient for timber; must be FSC plus PEFC dual certification
No — BES 6001 'Good' rating for concrete is below threshold for Credit 1
Yes — all major materials carry recognised responsible sourcing certifications
Partially — credits for steel and timber but not concrete

answer.rationale: Mat 03 Credit 1 requires responsible sourcing certifications for major materials. BES 6001 (any rating), FSC and PEFC are all recognised standards; the credit recognises certified sourcing rather than requiring a specific BES rating.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Mat 03

question.text: An industrial warehouse development in Doncaster targets Wst 01 (Construction Waste Management) under BREEAM NC 2018. The project produces 8.2 tonnes of construction waste per 100m² of constructed floor area, of which 75% is diverted from landfill (recycled or reused). A Site Waste Management Plan was implemented from Stage 2 onwards. Does this scheme qualify for Wst 01 Credit 1?
options: No — waste rate must be below 6 tonnes/100m² for any credit
Yes — waste generation below 13 tonnes/100m² and 70%+ diversion meets Credit 1
No — diversion must be 90%+ to qualify
Partially — waste generation credit qualifies but not the diversion credit

answer.rationale: Wst 01 Credit 1 in BREEAM NC 2018 requires construction waste generation below threshold (varies by building type — typically ~13 t/100m² for industrial) and 70% diversion from landfill plus implementation of a Site Waste Management Plan.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wst 01

question.text: A new university teaching block in Sheffield is targeting LE 04 (Ecological change and enhancement) under BREEAM NC 2018, assessed via the Comprehensive route (Route 2). The LE 03 prerequisite criterion has been achieved and compliance with relevant ecology legislation is monitored. What is the maximum number of credits available to this project under LE 04?
options: 1 credit — Change and enhancement of ecology only
4 credits — one for Ecological enhancement plus up to three for Change and enhancement of ecology
2 credits — one for the prerequisite and one for enhancement
3 credits — the Comprehensive route caps LE 04 at three

answer.rationale: LE 04 is split into a prerequisite (Managing negative impacts on ecology, which awards no credits) and two credit-bearing parts. Table 11.3 gives the split by assessment route: on the Comprehensive route, Ecological enhancement is worth one credit and Change and enhancement of ecology up to three, so four in total. On the Foundation route, Ecological enhancement is not available and Change and enhancement is worth one credit.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, LE 04 Ecological change and enhancement, Table 11.3

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new healthcare building in central London targets Pol 04 (Reduction of Night Time Light Pollution) under BREEAM NC 2018. External lighting is designed to meet ILE Guidance Notes for the reduction of obtrusive light, with all external luminaires turned off automatically between 23:00 and 07:00 except where essential for safety. Luminaires have upward light ratio of 0% and meet the limits for the relevant Environmental Zone (E3 — Suburban). Does this scheme qualify for Pol 04 Credit 1?
options: No — automatic switch-off must be from 22:00 not 23:00
Yes — ILE compliance, automatic switch-off and zero upward light meets Credit 1
Partially — ILE compliance qualifies but switch-off timing does not
No — environmental zone E3 is too lenient; only E1 or E2 qualifies for the credit

answer.rationale: Pol 04 Credit 1 requires compliance with the relevant ILE/ILP guidance notes for the project's Environmental Zone, automatic luminaire switch-off during night hours (typically 23:00-07:00), and limits on obtrusive light. The conditions described comprehensively meet these requirements.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Pol 04

question.text: A new prison facility in the East Midlands is targeting Hea 06 (Security of site and building) under BREEAM NC 2018. A Suitably Qualified Security Specialist was appointed and carried out an evidence-based Security Needs Assessment at RIBA Stage 4 (Technical Design). The resulting security controls were incorporated into the as-built development. Does this scheme qualify for the Hea 06 credit?
options: Yes — the credit turns on implementation of the controls, not on when the assessment was carried out
No — the Security Needs Assessment must be conducted during or prior to Concept Design
Yes — prisons are assessed under a bespoke route where the timing criterion does not apply
Partially — one credit is available where the assessment is late but the controls are implemented

answer.rationale: Hea 06 has one part, Security of site and building, worth one credit. Criterion 1 requires the Suitably Qualified Security Specialist to conduct the evidence-based Security Needs Assessment during or prior to Concept Design, so that the controls developed from it can shape the proposals rather than being retrofitted. An assessment at RIBA Stage 4 fails that timing requirement even though the controls were implemented.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Hea 06 Security of site and building, criteria 1-3

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A speculative office in Birmingham targets Ene 04 (Low Carbon Design) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design includes a 60 kWp roof-mounted PV array providing approximately 6% of the building's annual regulated energy demand, and a feasibility study for further low-carbon technologies was completed at RIBA Stage 2 by a suitably qualified consultant. Does this scheme qualify for Ene 04 Credit 1?
options: No — feasibility study must be at Stage 3 not Stage 2
Yes — feasibility study and PV installation together earn the first credit
Partially — credit for feasibility but not for PV installation
Yes but only if PV provides 10% or more of annual regulated energy

answer.rationale: Ene 04 Credit 1 awards for a Low Zero Carbon (LZC) feasibility study completed by a suitably qualified consultant by Concept Design. A second credit may require a specific LZC contribution threshold (often around 10%), but the first credit recognises the feasibility study and installation of the recommended LZC measure.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Ene 04

question.text: A residential refurbishment in central Edinburgh targets Mat 01 (Environmental Impact from Construction Products — Building Life Cycle Assessment) under BREEAM RFO 2014. The project undertook a streamlined LCA using IMPACT-compliant software at RIBA Stage 3, comparing the design against a benchmark and identifying a 12% reduction in cradle-to-grave embodied carbon. The LCA was reviewed and verified by a third party. Does this scheme qualify for Mat 01 Credit 1?
options: No — LCA must be from RIBA Stage 2 to qualify
Partially — credits for LCA process but not for the reduction quantum
No — minimum 20% embodied carbon reduction required for Credit 1
Yes — IMPACT-compliant LCA at Stage 3 with verified reduction meets Credit 1

answer.rationale: Mat 01 Credit 1 in BREEAM RFO 2014 awards for an LCA undertaken using IMPACT-compliant software (or equivalent) by Concept Design (typically Stage 3 acceptable for early credits). The first credit recognises the LCA process and the design improvement demonstrated, not a specific reduction threshold.
answer.citation: BREEAM RFO 2014, Mat 01

question.text: A new mixed-use development in Cambridge with offices, retail and residential is being assessed under BREEAM NC 2018. The Project Manager has appointed a BREEAM AP (Accredited Professional) at Concept Design stage and engaged a Sustainability Champion within the design team who has formal BREEAM training. The BREEAM AP attended all design team meetings through to Concept Design completion. Does this scheme qualify for Man 01 (Project Brief and Design) Credit 1?
options: No — BREEAM AP must be a registered architect
No — must demonstrate consultation with future occupants/end users
Yes — AP appointment, training, and design team integration meets Credit 1
Partially — credit for AP appointment but consultation must extend beyond Concept Design

answer.rationale: Man 01 Credit 1 requires demonstration of stakeholder consultation including future occupants or end-user representatives during early-stage design, beyond the appointment of a BREEAM AP. AP appointment supports other Man credits but does not on its own satisfy Man 01 Credit 1.

question.text: A new secondary school in Leeds is targeting Man 01 (Project Brief and Design) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design team appointed a BREEAM AP at RIBA Stage 3, ran a single project delivery workshop with the contractor and architect at Stage 4, and consulted with the headteacher and governors but did not engage pupils or the local community. Does this scheme qualify for the first two credits under Man 01 (Project delivery planning and Stakeholder consultation - project delivery)?
options: Yes — BREEAM AP appointment and stakeholder workshop satisfy both credits
No — BREEAM AP must be appointed by end of RIBA Stage 2 (Concept Design)
No — third-party (community/end-user) consultation is mandatory for Stakeholder consultation credit
Partially — Project delivery planning qualifies but not Stakeholder consultation

answer.rationale: Man 01 requires the BREEAM AP to be appointed before the end of RIBA Stage 2 (Concept Design) to influence the Strategic Brief and Concept Design. Appointment at Stage 3 is too late to claim the Project delivery planning credit.

question.text: A speculative office development in Birmingham is targeting Man 02 (Life Cycle Cost and Service Life Planning) under BREEAM NC 2018. The client commissioned an elemental Life Cycle Cost analysis at RIBA Stage 2 covering construction, operation, maintenance and replacement over a 60-year period, including envelope, services and finishes. The LCC was updated at Stage 4 to reflect detailed design. Does this scheme qualify for the first two credits under Man 02?
options: No — LCC must be completed at RIBA Stage 1 (Preparation and Brief)
No — LCC must cover a minimum 25-year period only, not 60
Yes — elemental LCC at Stage 2, 60-year period, and Stage 4 update meets requirements
No — component-level (not elemental) LCC is required for the second credit

answer.rationale: Man 02 requires an elemental LCC at Concept Design (Stage 2) over a minimum period (typically 60 years for building, 25 for components), covering capital, operational, maintenance and replacement costs, with updates at later stages. The described approach meets the first two credits.

question.text: A new hospital wing in Bristol is targeting Man 03 (Responsible Construction Practices) under BREEAM NC 2018. The principal contractor is registered with the Considerate Constructors Scheme and achieved a CCS score of 35/50. They monitor and report energy (kWh), water (m³), and transport-related CO2 from construction, and have an ISO 14001 EMS covering the site. Does this scheme qualify for the Considerate construction credit (2 credits available)?
options: No — minimum CCS score of 40/50 required for two credits, only one awarded at 35
Yes — CCS score of 35 awards both Considerate construction credits
No — CCS registration alone qualifies; the score is not used in BREEAM
No — only ISO 14001 evidence is required, CCS is not recognised

answer.rationale: Man 03 awards Considerate construction credits based on CCS score thresholds: typically one credit at a score of 35 and two credits at 40 or above. A score of 35 qualifies for one credit only.

question.text: A new mixed-use residential and retail scheme in Glasgow targets Man 04 (Commissioning and Handover) under BREEAM NC 2018. A specialist commissioning manager was appointed at RIBA Stage 4 to develop the commissioning programme. The MEP systems were commissioned per BSRIA BG 49/2015 and CIBSE Commissioning Codes. Seasonal commissioning is contractually committed for 12 months post-handover. A Building User Guide has been produced for residents and retail tenants. Does this scheme qualify for the Commissioning and testing credit and the Handover credit?

No — Building User Guide must be available before practical completion, not after
No — seasonal commissioning must extend to 24 months post-handover
No — commissioning manager must be appointed by end of RIBA Stage 2

answer.rationale: Man 04 requires a specialist commissioning manager appointed in time to influence design (Stage 4 is acceptable for complex systems), commissioning to BSRIA/CIBSE codes, seasonal commissioning over 12 months, and a Building User Guide tailored to occupants. All criteria are met.

question.text: A new university research building in Cambridge targets Man 05 (Aftercare) under BREEAM NC 2018. However, no post-occupancy evaluation (POE) is planned and energy/water consumption will not be monitored for the first 12 months. Does this scheme qualify for all three Man 05 credits (Aftercare support, Seasonal commissioning, Post-occupancy evaluation)?
options: Yes — aftercare team and walkround satisfy all three Man 05 credits
Partially — Aftercare support and Seasonal commissioning qualify, POE does not
No — Man 05 requires 24 months of aftercare to qualify for any credit
No — only the Aftercare support credit qualifies; seasonal commissioning and POE credits are not met

answer.rationale: Man 05 has three separate credit areas. The aftercare team and 3-month walkround meet Aftercare support, but seasonal commissioning (12-month monitoring of energy/water) and POE (formal post-occupancy evaluation exercise) are explicitly not provided, so only one of three credits is achieved.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Man 05 Aftercare

Yes — but only if the sustainability manager is also a chartered engineer or architect

question.text: A new primary school in Sheffield targets Hea 01 (Visual Comfort) under BREEAM NC 2018. The classrooms achieve an average daylight factor of 2.1% with a minimum point daylight factor of 0.6%, view out is provided from 95% of seated positions to within 7m of a window, and all teaching spaces have manual blinds for glare control. Internal and external lighting comply with the relevant CIBSE/SLL codes. Does this scheme qualify for the daylighting credit under Hea 01?
options: No — schools require minimum 80% of floor area to achieve the daylight factor, not classrooms only
No — minimum point daylight factor must be at least 0.9% in education buildings
Partially — qualifies for view out but not the daylighting credit
Yes — daylight factor, view out, glare control and lighting design all meet the criteria

answer.rationale: Hea 01 daylighting for education buildings requires an average daylight factor of 2% and a minimum point of 0.6% across 80% of the relevant floor area. With ADF 2.1%, minimum 0.6%, compliant view out (within 7m) and glare control, the credit is achieved.

question.text: A new speculative office in Leeds targets Hea 01 (Visual Comfort) under BREEAM NC 2018. Yes — high-frequency ballasts alone are sufficient for the lighting credit
No — lighting zoning must be a maximum of one workstation per zone

question.text: A new primary school in Sheffield targets Ene 03 (External Lighting) under BREEAM NC 2018. The specified external lighting comprises LED luminaires with an average luminous efficacy of 65 lamp-lumens per circuit-watt across all external areas (car park, footpaths, playground floodlights). All luminaires are controlled by daylight sensors and time switches that automatically switch off when not required. Does this scheme qualify for the Ene 03 credit?
options: Partially — qualifies for controls but not efficacy
Yes — efficacy exceeds 60 lamp-lumens/W and controls are compliant
No — playground floodlights are excluded from the assessment
No — minimum efficacy under Ene 03 is 70 lamp-lumens/W

answer.rationale: Ene 03 requires the average initial luminous efficacy of external light fittings to be at least 60 lamp-lumens per circuit-watt, and that lighting is controlled for presence and daylight where applicable. Both criteria are satisfied.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Ene 03 External Lighting

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.review_notes: Verified: BREEAM NC 2018 Ene 03 raised minimum luminous efficacy threshold to 70 lamp-lumens/W (from 60 in NC 2014). At 65 lm/W the scheme falls short.

question.text: A new speculative office in Bristol with no cold storage or refrigeration plant beyond standard tea-point fridges is being assessed under BREEAM NC 2018. The assessor is reviewing Ene 05 (Energy Efficient Cold Storage). Does this scheme qualify for Ene 05 credits?
options: No — credit is filtered out as not applicable; no credits available or required
No — must install A+++ rated fridges to claim the credit
Yes — standard domestic-style fridges count as qualifying cold storage
Yes — default award of one credit applies to all office schemes

answer.rationale: Ene 05 only applies where the building contains significant cold storage systems (e.g. supermarket refrigeration, large cold rooms). For schemes without such systems the credit is filtered out and not assessed — it does not award by default and does not penalise the scheme.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Ene 05 and Filtering Rules

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.primary: BREEAM NC 2018 SD5078, Ene 05 and Filtering Rules

question.text: A new 12-storey residential tower in Croydon is targeting Ene 06 (Energy Efficient Transportation Systems) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design includes two passenger lifts, but only an analysis of expected lift usage has been completed — no comparison between two or more lift specifications has been made, and no energy-efficient features (such as regenerative drives or standby mode) have been specified. Does this scheme qualify for any Ene 06 credits?
options: No — Ene 06 only applies to commercial buildings, not residential
Yes — usage analysis alone awards the first credit
Yes — installation of any lift automatically awards one credit
No — must compare at least two transport system arrangements AND specify energy-efficient features

answer.rationale: Ene 06 requires both an analysis of transportation demand and counter-strategies AND a comparison of at least two types/specifications of transport system, selecting the arrangement with the lowest energy consumption, plus specification of three energy-efficient features. Without these the credits cannot be awarded.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Ene 06 Energy Efficient Transportation Systems

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new life sciences research building at a Cambridge university campus is targeting Ene 07 (Energy efficient laboratory systems) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design team engaged the client during preparation of the initial project brief to define laboratory performance criteria including purpose, occupant activities, containment requirements, system interaction and future flexibility; sized the ventilation supply and extract correctly; and demonstrated minimised laboratory energy demand. How is Ene 07 structured, and what has the team achieved so far?
options: Ene 07 has a containment prerequisite followed by one credit; the team has met the prerequisite only
Ene 07 offers a single credit for laboratory energy efficiency, which the team has achieved
Ene 07 is split into Design specification (one credit) and Best practice energy efficient measures (up to four credits, building type dependent); the team has met the Design specification criteria
Ene 07 is filtered out for university buildings and cannot be assessed here

answer.rationale: Ene 07 is split into two parts: Design specification, worth one credit, and Best practice energy efficient measures, worth up to four credits depending on building type. There is no prerequisite. The Design specification credit requires engagement with the client during preparation of the initial project brief to determine occupant requirements and define laboratory performance criteria, correct sizing of services equipment including ventilation supply and extract, and demonstration of minimised laboratory energy demand — all of which this team has done. The best-practice measures, such as variable air volume fume cupboards and ventilation heat recovery, are assessed separately for the remaining credits.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Ene 07 Energy efficient laboratory systems, criteria 1-3

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.primary: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Ene 07 Energy efficient laboratory systems, criteria 1-3

question.text: A new mid-market hotel in Birmingham targets Ene 08 (Energy Efficient Equipment) under BREEAM NC 2018. The specification includes A-rated commercial laundry equipment, ENERGY STAR rated kitchen appliances in the back-of-house, and a controls strategy for guest room TVs and minibars (master switch on room key card). However, the IT server room equipment has not yet been specified and will be procured by the operator post-handover. Does this scheme qualify for the Ene 08 credit?
options: Yes — all unregulated loads are addressed including server room by default
No — server room equipment must be specified at design stage to claim the credit
Yes — significant unregulated energy uses (laundry, catering, guest controls) are addressed with efficient equipment
No — Ene 08 requires every single appliance to be A+++ rated

answer.rationale: Ene 08 awards credit where the major unregulated energy-consuming equipment relevant to the building type has been identified and specified as energy efficient. For a hotel, laundry, catering and guest room controls are the key loads — server rooms are not a primary load for this typology and post-handover procurement does not invalidate the credit.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Ene 08 Energy Efficient Equipment

question.text: A new supermarket in Leeds is targeting Ene 05 (Energy efficient cold storage) under BREEAM NC 2018. The refrigeration system has been designed, installed and commissioned in accordance with the Code of Conduct for carbon reduction in the refrigeration retail sector and BS EN 378-2:2016, using components listed on the Enhanced Capital Allowance Energy Technology Product List, and commissioned in compliance with the Man 04 commissioning criteria. Does this scheme qualify for the refrigeration energy consumption credit under Ene 05?
options: No — the system must also demonstrate at least a 10% reduction against the BREEAM refrigeration energy benchmark
Yes — the credit is awarded on compliance with the Code of Conduct, BS EN 378-2:2016, use of ECA ETPL-listed components and Man 04 commissioning
No — CO2 transcritical systems are excluded from assessment under Ene 05
Partially — the credit is available only where waste heat reclaim is also installed

answer.rationale: Ene 05 is split into two parts, each worth one credit: Refrigeration energy consumption, and Indirect greenhouse gas emissions. The refrigeration energy consumption credit is compliance-based, not benchmark-based: criterion 1 requires the system to be designed, installed and commissioned in accordance with the Code of Conduct for carbon reduction in the refrigeration retail sector and BS EN 378-2:2016, using robust and tested systems or components on the Enhanced Capital Allowance Energy Technology Product List or equivalent, and criterion 2 requires commissioning in compliance with Man 04. BREEAM NC 2018 sets no percentage reduction against a refrigeration energy benchmark for this credit.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Ene 05 Energy efficient cold storage, criteria 1-2

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.primary: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Ene 05 Energy efficient cold storage, criteria 1-2

question.text: A new headquarters office in Leeds city centre is targeting Tra 01 (Transport assessment and travel plan) under BREEAM NC 2018. A site-specific transport assessment was undertaken at Concept Design covering existing and predicted travel patterns, the local pedestrian and cyclist environment, amenities within 500m, disabled access, calculation of the existing Accessibility Index, and current cyclist facilities. A site-specific travel plan was developed, the known occupier was involved, and building management has committed to implementing it. How many credits does this achieve under Tra 01?
options: 5 credits — the maximum available for an office building
1 credit — the second credit requires post-occupancy travel surveys
No credits — the Accessibility Index must be at least 8 for an office
2 credits — the maximum available under Tra 01

answer.rationale: Tra 01 in BREEAM NC 2018 is worth two credits in total, awarded for the transport assessment and travel plan together. The scheme meets criterion 1 (assessment and draft plan no later than Concept Design), the full scope of criterion 2 including the Accessibility Index calculation at 2.f, and criteria 3 to 5 on developing the plan, involving the occupier and demonstrating implementation. The Accessibility Index is calculated here as an input to Tra 02; it does not itself scale the Tra 01 award.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Tra 01 Transport assessment and travel plan, criteria 1-5

question.text: A new primary school in suburban Bristol is being assessed under BREEAM NC 2018. Within 500m safe walking distance the site has a local convenience store, a public outdoor open space, a post box and a cash machine; the nearest GP surgery is 900m away. The assessor asks whether the proximity of these amenities earns a credit in its own right. Which statement is correct?
options: Yes — a single credit is available where at least four amenities lie within 500m
Yes — but only for schools, where amenity proximity is separately assessed
No — reporting the number and type of accessible amenities within 500m is part of the Tra 01 transport assessment (criterion 2.d), not a standalone credit
No — amenity proximity was removed from BREEAM entirely and is not assessed in any form

answer.rationale: BREEAM NC 2018 has no separate proximity-to-amenities issue; the five transport issues of the previous scheme were consolidated into Tra 01 and Tra 02. Amenities survive as criterion 2.d of the Tra 01 transport assessment, which requires reporting of the number and type of existing accessible amenities within 500m of the site, against the list in Table 7.1. That reporting contributes to the Tra 01 award as a whole rather than earning a credit by itself.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Tra 01 Transport assessment and travel plan, criterion 2.d and Table 7.1

question.text: A new 4,000 m2 office development in Birmingham city centre is targeting Tra 02 (Sustainable transport measures) under BREEAM NC 2018. The Tra 01 prerequisite has been achieved. The existing Accessibility Index for the site is 7.5. Under Table 7.4, does the existing Accessibility Index itself score a point for this scheme?
options: No — an existing Accessibility Index of 8 or above is required for building types other than prisons, MOD sites, rural-location-sensitive buildings and group 3
Yes — any Accessibility Index above 4 scores the point for all building types
Yes — offices in a city centre are assessed against the reduced threshold of 4
No — the Accessibility Index is used only in Tra 01 and scores no points under Tra 02

answer.rationale: Table 7.4 option 1 awards one point where the existing Accessibility Index calculated in Tra 01 reaches at least 4 for prisons or MOD sites, rural-location-sensitive buildings and other building group 3, and at least 8 for all other building types. A city-centre office falls in the latter group, so an Accessibility Index of 7.5 falls short. The index is not irrelevant to Tra 02 though: it also sets which column of Table 7.3 converts the total points into credits.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Tra 02 Sustainable transport measures, Table 7.4 option 1

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new hospital wing in Sheffield is targeting Tra 01 (Transport assessment and travel plan) under BREEAM NC 2018. The project team commissioned a site-specific transport assessment and travel plan, but the assessment was carried out at RIBA Stage 4 (Technical Design), by which point the site layout and built form were fixed. Does this scheme qualify for the Tra 01 credits?
options: Yes — Tra 01 sets no timing requirement provided the assessment is site-specific
Partially — one of the two credits is available where the assessment is late
Yes — for healthcare buildings the assessment may be undertaken at any stage before handover
No — the transport assessment and draft travel plan must be undertaken no later than Concept Design, so they can demonstrably influence site layout and built form

answer.rationale: Criterion 1 of Tra 01 requires the site-specific transport assessment (or travel statement) and draft travel plan to be undertaken no later than Concept Design, and to be capable of demonstrably influencing the site layout and built form. An assessment produced at RIBA Stage 4, once layout and form are fixed, cannot meet that test, so neither Tra 01 credit is available — and because Tra 02 is prerequisite on Tra 01 criteria 3-5, the Tra 02 credits are also at risk.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Tra 01 Transport assessment and travel plan, criterion 1

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new mixed-use residential and retail scheme in Cardiff is targeting Tra 02 (Sustainable transport measures) under BREEAM NC 2018. The Tra 01 prerequisite has been achieved. The existing Accessibility Index is 2.8. The project team negotiates with the local bus operator and demonstrates an increase over the existing Accessibility Index through additional services. Under Table 7.4, how many points does that measure score?
options: 2 points — demonstrating an increase over the existing Accessibility Index through negotiation with bus, train or tram companies
1 point — all public transport measures score a single point each
No points — the existing Accessibility Index of 2.8 is too low for any transport measure to score
4 points — negotiated service increases are double-weighted in urban centres

answer.rationale: Table 7.4 lists the sustainable transport measures and their point values. Option 1, the existing Accessibility Index meeting its threshold, scores 1 point. Option 2, demonstrating an increase over the existing Accessibility Index through negotiation with local bus, train or tram companies to increase services, scores 2 points. The points from all implemented measures are then converted to credits through Table 7.3, using the column matching the site's Accessibility Index band.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Tra 02 Sustainable transport measures, Table 7.4 option 2

question.text: A new build secondary school in Leeds targets Wat 02 (Water Monitoring) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design specifies a pulsed-output water meter on the mains supply connected to the BMS, plus sub-meters with pulsed output on the sports hall changing block (high water-use area) and the science block. All sub-meters report to the BMS for leak identification and consumption analysis. Does this scheme qualify for the Wat 02 credit?
options: Yes — main meter with BMS connection and sub-metering of high water-consuming areas meets the criteria
No — sub-meters must be installed on every individual WC group, not just high water-use areas
No — Wat 02 requires ultrasonic flow meters rather than pulsed-output meters
Partially — only the main meter qualifies; sub-meters are a separate Wat 03 requirement

answer.rationale: Wat 02 requires a water meter with pulsed output on the mains supply (or each supply) connected to a BMS or other monitoring system, and sub-metering of water-consuming plant or building areas with consumption above a defined threshold. The sports/changing and science blocks qualify as high-consumption areas.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wat 02 Water Monitoring

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new logistics warehouse in Milton Keynes targets Wat 03 (Water Leak Detection) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design includes a flow-based leak detection system on the mains supply between the utility connection and the building, capable of detecting major leaks based on continuous flow and abnormal pressure. However, no flow control device has been specified on each WC area to shut off supply when unoccupied. Does this scheme qualify for both available credits under Wat 03?
options: Yes — both credits are met as the mains leak detection is sufficient for the second credit
No — only the first credit (leak detection system) is met; the second credit requires flow control on sanitary supplies
No — neither credit is met as a BMS-connected detection system is mandatory
Partially — qualifies for the second credit only as the first credit requires zonal detection

answer.rationale: Wat 03 awards one credit for a leak detection system on the mains supply between the utility connection and the building, and a second credit for flow control devices that regulate water supply to each WC area/facility based on occupancy. Without the WC-zone flow control, only the first credit is achieved.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wat 03 Water Leak Detection

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new commercial laundry serving a hotel chain, located in Bristol, targets Wat 04 (Water Efficient Equipment) under BREEAM NC 2018. The specification includes high-efficiency continuous-batch washing machines with water recycling achieving 4 L/kg dry weight (versus a typical 12 L/kg baseline), and a vehicle wash facility with water reclaim recovering 70% of water used. No other unregulated water uses are present. Does this scheme qualify for both available Wat 04 credits?
options: No — Wat 04 only applies to irrigation systems, not industrial process water
Yes — water-efficient equipment is specified for all identified unregulated water-consuming processes on site
Partially — only the laundry equipment qualifies; vehicle wash is excluded from Wat 04
No — vehicle wash reclaim must achieve at least 80% recovery to qualify

answer.rationale: Wat 04 awards credits for specifying water-efficient equipment that reduces unregulated water consumption. Commercial laundry equipment and vehicle wash systems are both listed as eligible processes. Water-efficient laundry equipment and vehicle wash reclaim systems with recovery meeting the benchmark qualify for the available credits.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wat 04 Water Efficient Equipment

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new build residential apartment block in Southwark targets Wat 01 (Water Consumption) under BREEAM NC 2018. The specification includes 4 L/flush dual-flush WCs, 6 L/min shower heads, 4 L/min basin taps, A-rated dishwashers (10 L/cycle) and A-rated washing machines (7 L/kg). The BREEAM Wat 01 calculator returns a consumption figure of 95 L/person/day. Does this scheme qualify for 3 credits under Wat 01?
options: Partially — only 2 credits are awarded; the third requires rainwater or greywater recycling
Yes — 95 L/p/d falls within the 3-credit band for residential assessments
No — 3 credits requires consumption at or below 85 L/p/d for residential
No — Wat 01 caps at 2 credits for residential dwellings under NC 2018

answer.rationale: Wat 01 credits are awarded based on percentage improvement over a baseline (or absolute L/p/d figures). A consumption of around 95 L/p/d for residential typically falls within the 3-credit band (approximately 25–40% improvement over baseline), with sanitaryware and white goods both contributing.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wat 01 Water Consumption

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.review_notes: Three reviewers agree 95 L/p/d does not achieve 3 credits. Stored answer A is wrong. 3 credits typically requires <=85 L/p/d (with or without recycling depending on calculator route).

question.text: A new NHS acute hospital in Birmingham targets Wat 01 (Water Consumption) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design includes 4.5/3 L dual-flush WCs across patient wards, 6 L/min sensor-operated basin taps in clinical areas, and 8 L/min thermostatic showers in patient en-suites. Surgical scrub-up sinks and other clinical process water uses are excluded from the Wat 01 calculation. The calculator returns a 35% improvement over baseline. Does this scheme qualify for 4 credits under Wat 01?
options: Partially — credits are halved for healthcare due to infection control specification constraints
No — 4 credits requires at least 50% improvement over baseline
Yes — 35% improvement falls within the 4-credit band for healthcare assessments
No — only sanitary fittings serving staff and visitor WCs may be included; patient en-suite fittings are excluded

answer.rationale: Wat 01 awards up to five credits on a sliding scale set by Table 8.1: 12.5% improvement over the baseline for one credit, 25% for two, 40% for three, 50% for four, 55% for five, and 65% for the exemplary performance credit. A 35% improvement therefore achieves two credits, not four. Clinical process water is correctly excluded from the Wat 01 calculation.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Wat 01 Water consumption, Table 8.1

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new 14,000 m² office development in Leeds targets Mat 01 (Environmental Impacts from Construction Products – Building LCA) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design team commissions a full superstructure and substructure LCA using IMPACT-compliant software at RIBA Stage 2, comparing four design options and tracking the chosen option through to Stage 4. Reporting follows the LCA Reporting Format. Does this scheme qualify for the basic Mat 01 LCA credits?
options: No — Mat 01 requires LCA to commence at RIBA Stage 4 once design is fixed
No — only One Click LCA is accepted under Mat 01
Yes — early-stage LCA with options comparison using compliant tool meets Mat 01 criteria
Partially — qualifies for reporting credits but not options analysis credits

answer.rationale: Mat 01 (NC 2018) requires building LCA using a recognised IMPACT-compliant tool, conducted at early design stages (RIBA 2) with options appraisal, and reported in the LCA Reporting Format. Tracking through to Stage 4 supports superstructure/substructure credits.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Mat 01 Environmental Impacts from Construction Products

question.text: A new community sports centre in Coventry is targeting Mat 02 (Environmental impacts from construction products — Environmental Product Declarations) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design team specifies construction products whose EPDs give a total EPD points score of 24, and enters each EPD into the Mat 01/02 Results Submission Tool with its material category classification. Does this scheme qualify for the Mat 02 credit?
options: No — a total EPD points score of at least 40 is required
No — Mat 02 requires a BRE Green Guide A+ or A rating for at least 80% by cost of materials
Partially — the credit is prorated between 20 and 40 points
Yes — the credit requires a total EPD points score of at least 20, and the EPDs have been entered in the Mat 01/02 Results Submission Tool

answer.rationale: Mat 02 in BREEAM NC 2018 awards one credit for specifying construction products with a recognised Environmental Product Declaration. Criterion 1 requires a total EPD points score of at least 20, calculated by finding each EPD's points score in Table 9.8 and applying Table 9.9. Criterion 2 requires the details of each EPD to be entered into the Mat 01/02 Results Submission Tool, which verifies the score and the credit award. The BRE Green Guide rating route belongs to the previous version of the scheme.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Mat 02 Environmental impacts from construction products — EPD, criteria 1-2

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new mixed-use development in Bristol targets Mat 03 (Responsible Sourcing of Construction Products) under BREEAM NC 2018. The structural frame is CLT timber certified to FSC, brick cladding is BES 6001 'Very Good', concrete blocks have BES 6001 'Pass', plasterboard has no certification, and steel reinforcement is BES 6001 'Excellent'. The contractor calculates a weighted RSCP score across all applicable materials. Are these specifications consistent with achieving at least the first Mat 03 credit?
options: No — BES 6001 'Pass' is not recognised under Mat 03
Yes — uncertified products simply score zero in the weighted calculation; the mix can still reach the threshold
No — any uncertified product (plasterboard) disqualifies all Mat 03 credits
Filter out — Mat 03 does not apply where CLT is used

answer.rationale: Mat 03 uses a weighted RSCP scoring system; uncertified products contribute zero points but do not disqualify the credit. BES 6001 ratings from Pass to Outstanding all score, and FSC/PEFC chain-of-custody for timber is recognised. The aggregate score determines credits awarded.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Mat 03 Responsible Sourcing of Construction Products

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new primary school in Norwich targets Mat 04 (Insulation) under BREEAM NC 2018. The insulation specification covers external walls (mineral wool, A+ Green Guide), roof (PIR, A rating), ground floor (XPS, B rating), and building services (phenolic, A rating). The design team calculates an Insulation Index using embodied impact × thermal performance, and the responsible sourcing of each insulation product is verified via BES 6001 certificates. Does this scheme qualify for both Mat 04 credits?
options: Yes — Insulation Index is a weighted calculation; both embodied impact and responsible sourcing credits can be achieved
No — XPS at B rating disqualifies the Insulation Index credit
Partially — only the responsible sourcing credit qualifies, not the Insulation Index
No — Mat 04 requires all insulation to be A+ rated

answer.rationale: Mat 04 awards credits via the Insulation Index (a weighted calculation of embodied impact relative to thermal resistance and volume) and via responsible sourcing of insulation products. Lower-rated products do not disqualify; they reduce the Index score. Both credits are achievable with the specification described.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Mat 04 Insulation

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.unverifiable_reason: The scenario asks whether the scheme qualifies for 'both Mat 04 credits' under BREEAM NC 2018. SD5078 contains Mat 01, Mat 02, Mat 03, Mat 05 and Mat 06 — there is no Mat 04. It was a BREEAM 2014 issue, removed in the 2018 scheme, where insulation is assessed under Mat 01 (life cycle impacts) and Mat 03 (responsible sourcing). The premise is wrong rather than the keyed option, so the question cannot be corrected by re-keying. Scheduled for rewrite in v2.

question.text: A new logistics warehouse in Milton Keynes targets Mat 05 (Designing for Durability and Resilience) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design provides bollards at vehicle loading bays, impact-resistant kickplates to high-traffic doors, hard-wearing floor finishes in goods areas, and external wall protection where HGVs manoeuvre. No durability and resilience study covering material degradation from environmental/weather effects is undertaken. Does this scheme qualify for the Mat 05 credit?
options: No — Mat 05 requires both protection against material degradation AND protection against accidental damage in high-traffic areas
No — Mat 05 only applies to residential buildings
Partially — half a credit is awarded for impact protection only
Yes — protection from vehicle and trolley impacts alone meets Mat 05 criteria

answer.rationale: Mat 05 requires demonstration of design measures addressing BOTH (a) protection of exposed parts from material degradation due to environmental factors (UV, wind-driven rain, freeze-thaw etc.) AND (b) protection against accidental impact damage in vulnerable/high-traffic areas. Omitting the degradation assessment forfeits the credit.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Mat 05 Designing for Durability and Resilience

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

question.text: A new university teaching block in Sheffield targets Mat 06 (Material Efficiency) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design team produces a report at RIBA Stage 2 identifying material optimisation opportunities (column grid rationalisation, post-tensioned slabs to reduce concrete volume, off-site prefabrication of bathroom pods), implements three of these at Stage 4, and confirms implementation at Stage 5 (handover). Does this scheme qualify for the Mat 06 credit?
options: No — Mat 06 requires a quantitative kg/m² material reduction target to be met
Yes — identifying, implementing and confirming material efficiency opportunities across key RIBA stages meets Mat 06
No — Mat 06 requires opportunities to be identified at RIBA Stage 0/1, not Stage 2
Filter out — Mat 06 only applies to refurbishment projects

answer.rationale: Mat 06 awards the credit where opportunities to optimise material use are investigated and reported during concept/developed design (RIBA 2–3), implemented through technical design (Stage 4), and the implementation confirmed at construction/handover. No specific kg/m² target is mandated.

question.text: A new care home in Exeter targets Mat 03 (Responsible Sourcing) under BREEAM NC 2018. The specification includes structural timber from a supplier with FSC chain-of-custody, aggregates from a quarry with ISO 14001 only (no BES 6001), bricks with BES 6001 'Good', and aluminium curtain walling with BES 6001 'Very Good'. The contractor provides certificates at handover but did not include responsible sourcing requirements in the procurement specification or tender documents. Does this scheme qualify for the first Mat 03 credit?
options: Yes — what matters is the certificates obtained, not when responsible sourcing was specified
No — ISO 14001-only aggregates count as uncertified and disqualify all Mat 03 credits
No — Mat 03 requires responsible sourcing to be embedded in the procurement/tender documentation from the outset (Pre-requisite)
Yes — provided the weighted score reaches the first credit threshold

question.text: A new secondary school in Bristol targets Wst 03 (Operational Waste) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design includes a dedicated, accessible internal waste storage area of 12 m² with clearly labelled containers for general waste, paper/card, glass, plastic/metal, and food waste, located adjacent to the kitchen with vehicle access for collection. Does this scheme qualify for the Wst 03 credit?
options: Partially — only qualifies where an external bin store is provided in addition
No — Wst 03 requires on-site composting or anaerobic digestion for food waste
No — minimum storage area for a school must be 25 m² regardless of pupil numbers
Yes — dedicated, sized, accessible storage segregating the main recyclable streams meets the criteria

answer.rationale: Wst 03 requires a dedicated space for the segregation and storage of operational recyclable waste streams, appropriately sized for the building type, accessible to users and collection vehicles, and with separate containers for the main waste streams. The described facility meets these requirements.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wst 03 Operational Waste

question.text: A new healthcare centre in Norwich targets Wst 05 (Adaptation to Climate Change) under BREEAM NC 2018. The design team commissions a climate change adaptation strategy appraisal at RIBA Stage 3 covering structural and fabric resilience to projected UKCP18 climate scenarios up to 2080, but the report's recommendations are only reviewed by the client without being incorporated into the design. Does this scheme qualify for the Wst 05 credit?
options: No — the appraisal must occur by RIBA Stage 2 and recommendations must be implemented
No — appraisal is required but recommendations must be implemented in the design
Yes — the appraisal report alone satisfies the Wst 05 criteria
Yes — RIBA Stage 3 is the latest stage permitted for the appraisal

answer.rationale: Wst 05 requires a systematic climate change adaptation strategy appraisal for structural and fabric resilience by Concept Design (RIBA Stage 2), and crucially that mitigation measures identified are implemented within the design. Producing the report without acting on its recommendations does not satisfy the credit.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Wst 05 Adaptation to Climate Change

question.text: A new office development in Leeds is built on a previously developed brownfield site (a former printworks) which a Suitably Qualified Ecologist has confirmed to be of low ecological risk. The project targets LE 02 (Ecological risks and opportunities) under BREEAM NC 2018 and proposes to use the Foundation route (Route 1). Is the Foundation route available to this project?
options: No — the Foundation route is available only to residential schemes
Yes — the Foundation route is available on sites of low ecological risk, judged by the ecology present prior to site works including clearance and preparation
No — brownfield sites must always use the Comprehensive route because of possible contamination
Yes — the Foundation route is available to any project that appoints a Suitably Qualified Ecologist

answer.rationale: LE 02 is split into Survey and evaluation, and Determining the ecological outcomes for the site, with two assessment routes whose criteria and available credits differ. The Foundation route (Route 1) is available only on sites of low ecological risk, judged by the nature of the ecology present prior to site works including site clearance and preparation activities. The Comprehensive route (Route 2) is available for all sites. A previously developed site confirmed as low ecological risk therefore qualifies for the Foundation route, though that route offers fewer credits under Table 11.1.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, LE 02 Ecological risks and opportunities, assessment routes and Table 11.1

question.text: A new mixed-use scheme in Cardiff specifies VRF heat pump systems serving offices using R-32 refrigerant (GWP 675), with automatic refrigerant leak detection on all systems above 5 kg charge and pump-down capability to an isolated section in the event of a leak. The project targets Pol 01 (Impact of Refrigerants) under BREEAM NC 2018. Does this scheme qualify for both Pol 01 credits?
options: No — refrigerants with GWP above 10 cannot achieve any Pol 01 credit
Yes — leak detection plus automatic refrigerant containment/pump-down qualifies both credits where GWP ≤ 2500
No — leak detection alone qualifies, but pump-down/recovery is not recognised under Pol 01
Yes — only the leak detection credit applies; the GWP credit requires natural refrigerants

answer.rationale: Pol 01 awards one credit for refrigerant leak detection and a second credit for automatic refrigerant pump-down to a separate storage vessel or isolated part of the system. R-32 has a GWP of 675, well below the 2500 cap implied by the BREEAM DELC CO2e calculation thresholds, so both credits are available where the leak detection and containment criteria are met.
answer.citation: BREEAM NC 2018 (SD5078), Pol 01 Impact of Refrigerants

rubric.criterion: Rationale shows understanding of credit criteria

source.unverifiable_reason: The keyed answer makes Pol 01 eligibility conditional on a refrigerant GWP threshold of 2500. SD5078 Pol 01 contains no such threshold: credits are awarded on direct effect life cycle emissions (DELC ≤100 or ≤1000 kgCO2-eq/kW) or on all refrigerants having GWP ≤10, with leak detection assessed separately. No option states the manual's position, so the question cannot be corrected by re-keying and is scheduled for removal or rewrite in v2.

question.text: A new residential care home in Sheffield is served entirely by direct electric heating and hot water (no combustion plant on site). The assessor is reviewing Pol 02 (Local air quality). Does this scheme qualify for the maximum Pol 02 credits?
options: No — at least one credit requires combustion plant below 40 mg/kWh NOx to demonstrate compliance
Partially — only one credit is available where there is no on-site combustion
Yes — schemes with no combustion space heating or DHW source achieve the maximum credits available
No — Pol 02 cannot be awarded where direct electric heating is used, as grid emissions are excluded

answer.rationale: Pol 02 Local air quality awards up to two credits. Criterion 1 awards them where all heating and hot water is supplied by non-combustion systems, for example powered only by electricity. Where combustion plant is installed, criterion 2 instead requires emissions not to exceed the levels in Tables 12.4 and 12.5 — for a gas boiler, 27 mg/kWh for one credit and 24 mg/kWh for two. A building with no combustion space heating or hot water source therefore takes the maximum credits by the first route.
answer.citation: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 (SD5078), Issue 3.0, Pol 02 Local air quality, criterion 1
